behaviour: Unit tests for the pure range model.
rules: 1. Import the helpers from "../src/textStyleRanges" and `import type { TextStyleRange } from "../src/types";`; no DOM, no API helper.

tests.name: normalize sorts, clamps and drops empty or style-less ranges
tests.given: unsorted ranges including one with start >= end, one with no colour and one ending past a text length of 10
tests.expect: sorted ranges clamped to 10 with the empty and style-less ones gone

tests.name: normalize merges adjacent ranges with identical style and resolves overlaps
tests.given: [0,3) red, [3,5) red, and [4,8) highlight yellow
tests.expect: [0,4) red, [4,5) red + yellow, [5,8) yellow

tests.name: applyTextStyle splits a range and keeps the other property
tests.given: [0,10) color red + highlight yellow, apply { color: blue } to [3,6)
tests.expect: [0,3) red+yellow, [3,6) blue+yellow, [6,10) red+yellow

tests.name: applyTextStyle with null removes only that property
tests.given: [0,10) red + yellow, apply { highlight: null } to [2,4) and separately { color: null } to [0,10)
tests.expect: the highlight is gone only on [2,4); the second call leaves only the yellow highlight

tests.name: applyTextStyle fills uncovered gaps
tests.given: no ranges, apply { highlight: yellow } to [2,5) of a length-8 text
tests.expect: [{ start: 2, end: 5, highlight: yellow }] with no color key

tests.name: diffText derives a single replacement
tests.given: pairs: identical strings; insertion in the middle; deletion at the end; replacement of a repeated character
tests.expect: null; { from, to: from, insertLength }; { from, to, insertLength: 0 }; a minimal edit that never has to < from

tests.name: shiftStyleRanges moves ranges after an insertion and keeps those before
tests.given: [0,2) and [5,8), insert 3 characters at 3

tests.name: insertion strictly inside a range extends it, at a boundary it does not
tests.given: [2,5), insert 1 character at 3, then separately at 2 and at 5

tests.name: deletion shrinks overlapping ranges and drops emptied ones
getStyledLines maps ranges across a soft wrap that dropped whitespace
tests.given: originalText "hello world", text "hello\nworld", range [4,7) red
tests.expect: line 0 runs "hell" plain and "o" red; line 1 runs "w" red and "orld" plain

tests.name: getStyledLines maps ranges across hard newlines and kept whitespace
tests.given:
originalText "ab
cd ef", text "ab
cd 
ef", range [1,7) highlight yellow
tests.expect: runs carry yellow on "b", "cd " and "e" with correct start offsets

tests.name: getStyledLines with no ranges returns one plain run per non-empty line
tests.given: text with an empty middle line
tests.expect: [[run], [], [run]] with color and highlight null

tests.name: getStyledRunPositions honours alignment and RTL
tests.given: widths [10, 20] in a box of width 100 for left, center, right and right+rtl

tests.name: getUniformRangeStyle reports a shared value only
tests.given: [0,4) red and [4,8) blue
tests.expect: red for [1,3); null for [2,6); null for a gap

tests.name: sanitizeStyleRanges drops malformed entries
tests.given: a string; and an array with non-integer offsets, a numeric colour, an entry with no colour and an out-of-bound end
tests.expect: null; only valid entries, clamped and normalised

rules: 1. Add `import { newElementWith } from "../src/mutateElement";`, `import { Scene } from "../src/Scene";`, `import { redrawTextBoundingBox } from "../src/textElement";` (merged into the existing textElement import) and `import { getStyledLines } from "../src/textStyleRanges";`.

2. Build a rectangle and a bound text "hello world foo" (containerId set, container boundElements pointing at it) with API.createElement, add styleRanges via newElementWith, and put both in `new Scene(syncInvalidIndices([...]))` (syncInvalidIndices imported from "../src/fractionalIndex"); resize by scene.mutateElement(container, { width }) then redrawTextBoundingBox(text, container, scene).

tests.name: re-wrapping a bound text at a new container width keeps its ranges
tests.given: a styled bound text in a wide container, then the container made narrow and the text redrawn
tests.expect: text now contains a soft line break, styleRanges are deep-equal to before, and getStyledLines places the styled run on the wrapped line holding those characters

tests.name: changing font size re-wraps without changing ranges
tests.given: the same bound text after newElementWith(text, { fontSize: 40 }) and redrawTextBoundingBox
tests.expect: styleRanges unchanged and the styled characters still map to a run with the range colour

behaviour: Restore keeps legacy text without ranges and sanitises malformed ranges.

tests.name: restores a legacy text element without a styleRanges key
tests.given: API.createElement text "legacy" (no styleRanges)
tests.expect: the restored element has no own property styleRanges

tests.name: sanitises malformed style ranges
tests.given: a text "abcdef" whose styleRanges is [{start:0,end:2,color:"red"},{start:1.5,end:3,color:"blue"},{start:3,end:99,highlight:"yellow"},{start:4,end:4,color:"red"},{start:0,end:1,color:5}]
tests.expect: styleRanges equal [{start:0,end:2,color:"red"},{start:3,end:6,highlight:"yellow"}]

tests.name: drops a styleRanges value that sanitises to nothing

behaviour: Reconciliation keeps a text element's ranges with the text of the winning version.
rules: 1. Build local and remote versions of one text element id with different originalText and styleRanges as plain objects with index "a0", version 2 vs 3, and call reconcileElements(local, remote as RemoteExcalidrawElement[], {} as AppState).

tests.name: the winning text version brings its own ranges
tests.given: local v2 "hello" with [0,5) red, remote v3 "hello world" with [6,11) blue
tests.expect: the reconciled element has remote originalText and remote styleRanges; with the versions swapped it has the local pair

tests.name: an edited local text keeps its ranges against a newer remote
tests.given: the same pair with localAppState.editingTextElement set to the local element
tests.expect: the local originalText and styleRanges are kept together

behaviour: SVG export writes tspans per run and highlight rects for styled text, and plain text exports without tspans.
rules: 1. Import newElementWith from "@excalidraw/element"; export with exportScene({ type: "svg", data: { elements, appState: getDefaultAppState(), files: {} }, config: { canvasBackgroundColor: false } }) and query the returned SVGSVGElement.

tests.name: exports styled text as tspans with per-run fill
tests.given: a text "hello world" (index a0, width/height set) with styleRanges [{start:6,end:11,color:"#e03131"}]
tests.expect: one <text> with two <tspan>s: "hello " with fill equal to the element strokeColor and "world" with fill "#e03131"

tests.name: exports a highlight rect behind a highlighted run
tests.given: the same text with [{start:0,end:5,highlight:"#ffec99"}]
tests.expect: a <rect> with fill "#ffec99" and height equal to the line height px, appearing before the <text> in its group

tests.name: plain text exports without tspans
tests.given: the existing testElements
tests.expect: the SVG contains a <text> and no <tspan>

behaviour: jsdom editor flow: select a sub-range, pick text colour and highlight, shift on typing, undo, and copy/paste styles.
rules: 1. render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />); create the text with API.createElement({ type: "text", text: "Bid request timeout" }), API.setElements, API.setSelectedElements, Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER), then `const editor = await getTextEditor();`.

2. Select a range with editor.setSelectionRange(start, end) followed by fireEvent.select(editor); pick colours with act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor | actionChangeBackgroundColor, "ui", { color })).

3. Type with updateTextEditor(editor, nextValue); read the element with API.getElement or h.elements; leave the editor with Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor) before undo/redo (Keyboard.undo / Keyboard.redo).

tests.name: a stroke pick on a selected range sets its text colour only
tests.given: free text being edited with [12,19) selected, stroke pick COLOR_PALETTE.red[4]
tests.expect: styleRanges equal [{ start: 12, end: 19, color: red }]; strokeColor, backgroundColor and currentItemStrokeColor unchanged

tests.name: a background pick on a selected range sets its highlight only
tests.given: the same text, [4,11) selected, background pick COLOR_PALETTE.yellow[1]
tests.expect: a range [4,11) with highlight yellow and no color; backgroundColor and currentItemBackgroundColor unchanged

tests.name: picking the element's stroke colour clears a range's text colour
tests.given: a red range then the same selection picked with the element strokeColor
tests.expect: no styleRanges entry carries a color

tests.name: a bound label's highlight does not change its container
tests.given: a rectangle with a bound text, editing the label with a sub-range selected, background pick
tests.expect: the label has the highlight range and the rectangle backgroundColor is unchanged

tests.name: typing before a range shifts it
tests.given: range [12,19) then the value changed to "A Bid request timeout"
tests.expect: the range becomes [14,21)

tests.name: with no selection the stroke pick changes strokeColor
tests.given: editing with a collapsed caret, stroke pick red
tests.expect: strokeColor is red and styleRanges is absent

tests.name: undo restores the previous ranges and redo re-applies them
tests.given: a range pick, then exit the editor, undo, redo
tests.expect: after undo no range carries the picked colour; after redo the range is back

tests.name: paste styles does not copy ranges
tests.given: a styled text A and a plain text B, copy styles from A (actionCopyStyles) and paste onto B (actionPasteStyles)
tests.expect: B has no styleRanges and A keeps its own
